title: How to write a proposal for a landscaping project
summary: Paste your project notes into ChatGPT and get a clear landscaping proposal. Check the scope and the price before you send it.

tests.prompt:
You help a landscaper write a project proposal. Draft only. Do not send it.

Fill in these details. If a line is blank, write UNKNOWN and do not guess.

Customer name: [CUSTOMER NAME]
Property address: [ADDRESS]
Project summary: [PROJECT]
Work in the proposal: [WORK]
What's not included: [NOT INCLUDED]
Materials, if you are supplying them: [MATERIALS]
Price: [PRICE]
Deposit: [DEPOSIT]
Start and finish window: [TIMELINE]
How long the proposal is good: [EXPIRATION]
Your name and business: [YOUR NAME]
Your phone: [YOUR PHONE]
Email or text: [CHANNEL]

Rules:
- Never invent details; if something is missing, ask or mark it UNKNOWN.
- Do not add plants, patios, irrigation, or lighting that are not in [WORK].
- Do not change the price or the deposit. Copy them exactly.
- Do not promise a bloom, a plant size, or a maintenance result you did not write down.
- Keep the tone plain and friendly, like a proposal a homeowner can walk the yard with.
- No pressure and no "this season only" language unless [EXPIRATION] has a date.

Output format:
Return these headings only:
Channel
Subject (NONE if this is a text)
Proposal (200 words or fewer for email, 100 words or fewer for a text)
The work
What's not included
Price and deposit
Timeline
Next step
Facts used
Unknown

setup.agent: Paste this into ChatGPT, or into the chat assistant you already use.
steps: After you walk the yard, write the customer name, address, a short project summary, the work, what's not included, materials you will supply, the price, the deposit, and the schedule.
Add how long the proposal is good, your name, phone, and whether this is an email or a text.
Open ChatGPT, paste the ChatGPT prompt, and replace every [BRACKET]. Type UNKNOWN if a plant list or a date is not ready.
Check the work list, the price, and the deposit against your notes. Delete any patio, irrigation, or plant that was not in the walkthrough.
Paste the proposal into email or a PDF and send it yourself.
setup.approvalStep: You check the scope, the materials, and the price against your walkthrough notes, then you send the proposal yourself.
failureModes: The draft adds a patio, lighting, or irrigation you did not quote. Take those items out.
The price or deposit does not match your numbers. Copy your figures exactly.
Plant names or sizes appear that you did not specify. Keep the materials list to what you wrote.
The schedule promises a start week you cannot keep. Use only the window on your note.

faq.q: The homeowner also asked about a patio. Should I include it?
faq.a: Only if you priced it and put it in [WORK]. Otherwise leave it under What's not included and offer a separate proposal later so the totals stay clean.

faq.q: I have not chosen the plants yet. Can I still send a proposal?
faq.a: You can describe the beds in general terms and leave [MATERIALS] blank or marked UNKNOWN, then follow up with a plant list. Do not let the draft invent plant names or counts.

faq.q: Should I attach photos or a sketch?
faq.a: Yes if you have them. This prompt writes the words. You can attach your photos or a simple sketch when you send the email.

job: Paste a yard walkthrough and get a clear landscaping project proposal.
who: Landscapers and landscape companies who quote backyard projects and want a plain proposal that lists the work, the price, and what is not included.

example.scenario: A landscaper is proposing a front-bed refresh with new shrubs, mulch, and edging, not a full redesign.
example.input:
Customer name: Morgan Blake
Property address: 9 Lake Court
Project summary: Refresh the two front beds, keep the existing trees
Work in the proposal: Remove tired shrubs, plant eight boxwoods and twelve perennials, install steel edging, and spread three yards of brown mulch
What's not included: Irrigation, lighting, lawn seeding, and the backyard
Materials, if you are supplying them: Boxwoods, perennials, steel edging, and brown hardwood mulch
Price: $3,150
Deposit: $1,000 to book
Start and finish window: The week of April 6, two days on site
How long the proposal is good: 30 days
Your name and business: Riley at Green Thread Landscapes
Your phone: 555-0166
Email or text: email
example.output:
Channel: email
Subject: Landscaping proposal for 9 Lake Court

Proposal:
Hi Morgan, this is Riley at Green Thread Landscapes. Here is the proposal to refresh the two front beds at 9 Lake Court and keep the existing trees.

The work: Remove the tired shrubs, plant eight boxwoods and twelve perennials, install steel edging, and spread three yards of brown hardwood mulch. We supply the plants, edging, and mulch.

What's not included: Irrigation, lighting, lawn seeding, and any work in the backyard.

Price and deposit: The project is $3,150. A $1,000 deposit books the week of April 6. We expect two days on site. This proposal is good for 30 days.

Timeline: Week of April 6, two days on site.

Next step: Reply or call 555-0166 if you would like to book, and I can walk the beds with you once more before we start.

Facts used: 9 Lake Court, eight boxwoods, twelve perennials, three yards of mulch, $3,150, $1,000, week of April 6.
Unknown: none.
example.notes: Made-up project details, only to show a clear landscaping proposal.
